summary: This standards-track document describes methods for carrying PostScript in both MIME and X.400 mail systems and for converting between them.

eli5.summary: Sending a printable page description through two different mail systems.

questions: convert postscript between mime and x.400
subtitle: Two ways to carry PostScript through X.400 mail, and how each maps to MIME's application/postscript.

tldr.problem: PostScript documents sent by mail needed a defined carrier in X.400 and a defined mapping to and from MIME.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC describes an Extended Body Part and an FTAM body part (FTBP) for PostScript in X.400, each mapped to the MIME type application/postscript with no conversion.
tldr.outcome: Both representations are a single stream of octets copied as is. The FTAM method is the recommended one.

today: RFC 2160 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Two Mail Systems, Two Carriers
sections.content:
This document describes how to carry PostScript in the two standard mail systems, MIME and X.400, and how to convert between them. It follows the notation of RFC 2157 and the conversion rules of RFC 2156.

Two X.400 methods exist: an Extended Body Part, originally described in RFC 1494, and the FTAM Body Part. The FTAM method is recommended.
sections.eli5: There are two ways to put a page into the older mail system. One of them is the better choice.

sections.title: The X.400 Body Parts
sections.content:
The Extended Body Part postscript-body-part has no parameters and holds an OCTET STRING. Its identifier is mime-postscript-body, defined as { mixer-bp-data 2 }. This carries forward the work of RFC 1494, now that it is obsoleted by RFC 2157.

The PostScript FTBP is identified by setting FileTransferParameters.environment.application-reference to id-mime-ftbp-postscript, defined as { mixer-bp-data 6 }.
sections.eli5: Each carrier has its own numbered label, so the receiving system knows the contents are PostScript.

sections.title: Mapping to MIME
sections.content:
In MIME, PostScript travels as the application/PostScript body part, defined in RFC 1521.

Both X.400 forms are mapped to application/postscript with conversion type "No conversion". Each representation holds one stream of octets, which can be copied between them with no problems, and no other data needs converting. The RFC also gives the ASN.1 module with both OID assignments.
sections.eli5: The page is just a long string of bytes in both systems, so it is moved across exactly as it is.

sections.title: Security and Trademark
sections.content:
The security issues of PostScript are discussed in RFC 2046, and this memo identifies no additional ones.

The RFC also notes that PostScript is a trademark of Adobe Systems, Inc.
sections.eli5: The note points to an older document for safety advice and adds nothing new.

references.text: Kille, S., "MIXER: Mapping between X.400 and RFC 822/MIME", RFC 2156, January 1998.
Alvestrand, H., "Mapping between X.400 and RFC 822/MIME Message Bodies", RFC 2157, January 1998.
